# Student-life ComfyUI assets and live game verification

> **For agentic workers:** Use subagent-driven-development for independent art preparation and offline repair analysis. The root agent exclusively controls the live Unity Editor and applies reviewed changes.

**Goal:** Continue the approved school pixel style with design-driven environment props generated by ComfyUI, connect useful assets to existing data/placement flows, repair blockers exposed by real play, and verify the saved result.

**Architecture:** Reuse the approved school pack and installed Modern assets. Generate six distinct story/career props using a real ComfyUI sampler on FEVM, preserving prompts, guide/reference roles, raw outputs and postprocessing provenance. Import accepted art through Unity Editor APIs with explicit pivots and floor/support footprints; retain data-driven definitions and local Addressables. Avoid adding speculative story mechanics.

**Tech Stack:** Existing FEVM ComfyUI Qwen Image Edit or installed SDXL pixel model; Unity 6000.3.13f1, existing ResourceManager and FurnitureDefinition systems, native Windows UI input plus EditMode/PlayMode tests.

## Authorization and scope

The user reopened farmer after reboot and explicitly requested autonomous continuation based on the design documents. This supersedes the previous temporary restriction on foreground testing. Work in the user's open farmer checkout on town-playable-baseline-recovery; creating a separate checkout would not test their current Unity state. Preserve unrelated dirty files and back up any targeted House repair. No new character art, no canonical lore text, no external publishing or messages, no interruption of other ComfyUI jobs.

## Applied work and evidence

- Accepted `revision-03`: FEVM ComfyUI Qwen Image Edit, seed 2710202602, 20 steps, actual diffusion execution 495.491 seconds. Workflow, raw sheet, references, hashes and extraction scripts are preserved. All 41 manifest files were checked and mirrored to FEVM. The first clipped candidate was rejected; matching reference/latent dimensions resolved that failure.
- Six native sprites, two transparent floor adapters, two furniture definitions and two tiles. Label `StudentLifePixels` has 12 logical Addressables. Native art uses 48 PPU, Point filtering, no mipmaps, binary alpha and bottom contact pivots. Adapters preserve every native pixel and use the placement grid's 24,24 pixel anchor; footprints are 1x1 and 2x1. Wall and tabletop assets do not add floor occupancy.
- `StudentLifePixelReview.unity` composes all six with the approved school environment. Normal `Town -> HouseInterior` routing is preserved; the saved room gains a toy kitchen and snack crate with separate shallow ground colliders and foot-based depth sorting. The travelling player's depth band is scoped to HouseInterior, restoring original group enabled/order outside it. The saved direct-Play player persists its original no-group fallback as well. This avoids drawing the player over Town roofs/foreground layers.
- Repaired missing persistent floor/wall references in the separate `House` construction scene and its runtime tile set, preserving tile positions and collision layout. Existing unrelated legacy decorative missing references remain outside this repair.
- Fixed full-footprint placement preview validation and matching availability count. Replaced the first-60-items palette cap with full-catalog name/ID search and a 20-button paged pool.
- Removed the empty stretched Town HUD image and obsolete blank QuestLogPanel presentation. Tab journal opening/closing was verified with input; provider state is retained.
- `student-play-real-input.json`: 2/2 passed, including both props' mouse selection, exact occupied cells, save/clear/load/reload, and async Addressables loading/release. `school-play-final-green.json`: 4/4 passed, including existing school movement, collision, occlusion and desk persistence.
- Native Windows mouse/text search and crate placement: `evidence/native-palette.*`. The automated fixture's initial focus failure was caused by the repository-wide passive input test guard; the fixture now uses the existing real-input opt-out. Text is delivered through uGUI input events after mouse focus, never by assigning the search value or bypassing selection.
- Real Town/House door loop and saved prop verification: `evidence/house-reentry.*`. Keyboard input drove all movement without Transform writes. `house-prop-walk.txt` records player sorting behind (10250), at contact (10300) and in front (10376) of the kitchen (10312); matching Game View captures are retained.

- `focus-final-green.json`: 4/4 input regressions passed. Selected text fields own movement, camera, panel hotkeys and gather/interaction keys. Held key state is consumed so deselection does not replay a shortcut; normal controls resume afterward.
- `scoped-town-green.json`: 5/5 passed; `scope-play-final-green.json`: 2/2 passed, including persistent players, repeated active-scene transitions, existing group state, and serialized direct-House fallback. `house-scope-final-green.json`: 3/3 saved-scene checks passed. The rejected global sorting band and failed test-fixture attempts are retained as diagnostic evidence, not reported as final passes.

## Final verification

- Fresh Addressables content build succeeded with an empty error field in 285.574 seconds. Both `student-packed-green.json` (2/2) and `school-packed-green.json` (4/4) passed with Use Existing Build, verifying actual packed content loading and release. The editor was restored to its original Use Asset Database (fastest) mode afterward. Scene-authored sprite references remain ordinary serialized references; Addressables registration does not imply every scene sprite is loaded asynchronously.
- `final-verification.json` records 39 targeted passing tests: 27 EditMode and 12 PlayMode, zero failures among these selected final runs. This is not a claim that the entire project test suite passed.
- `final-saved-audit.txt` verifies all 13 newly added C# files are present in Unity compilation sources and all six review props retain persistent sprite references after reopening the saved scene.
- After the final sorting change, native Play Mode plus KeyboardState movement verified both normal `Boot -> Town -> HouseInterior -> Town` and direct `HouseInterior -> Town` entry routes. `evidence/final-live-scope.txt` records the House group enabled with depth ordering and the restored disabled/order-zero group in Town for both routes. Movement uses actual input and never writes player Transforms.
- `evidence/live-student-life-gameview.png` and `live-student-life-input.txt` preserve the final review-scene render and bounded D/W input. QA saves are isolated under this task's output directories; user save files are not used for placement tests.

## Inspecting the result and remaining scope

Open `Assets/Scenes/ArtReview/StudentLifePixelReview.unity` and press Play to inspect all six props in the approved school setting. In the separate `House` construction scene, search `studentlife` in the furniture palette to place the crate (1x1) and toy kitchen (2x1). The normal Boot/Single route retains Town's existing HouseInterior connection, where both floor props are also saved into the room.

No standalone player build or full-GDD completion is claimed. Existing character part slicing/initial avatar preview, the normal house entry camera showing the left map boundary, legacy palette icons, and unrelated decorative missing references remain follow-up work. No new character art was created.
